title: Tight And Self-Testing Multipartite Quantum Bell Inequalities From The Renormalization Group
authors: Paolo Abiuso, Julian Fischer, And Miguel Navascués
abstract:
Author(s): Paolo Abiuso, Julian Fischer, and Miguel Navascués

Attempts to understand multipartite quantum nonlocality are thwarted by the difficulty of devising quantum Bell inequalities (QBI) for systems composed of more than a few separate parties. In this Letter, we introduce the notion of tight connectors, a class of tensors which, if contracted according …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050204] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: Introduces tight connectors to construct tight multipartite quantum Bell inequalities via renormalization group, enabling self-testing of multipartite states.
motivation: Multipartite quantum nonlocality is hard to characterize due to the difficulty of devising quantum Bell inequalities for many parties.
method: Defines a class of tensors called tight connectors and shows that contracting them according to a renormalization group scheme yields tight multipartite quantum Bell inequalities.
result: Provides a systematic method to generate tight Bell inequalities for arbitrary numbers of parties, with self-testing properties.
conclusion: The approach advances the study of multipartite nonlocality and offers practical tools for quantum information tasks.

title: Boosting Work Extraction In Quantum Batteries Via Continuous Environment Monitoring
authors: Gabriele Cenedese, Giuliano Benenti, Dario Ferraro, And Marco G. Genoni
abstract:
Author(s): Gabriele Cenedese, Giuliano Benenti, Dario Ferraro, and Marco G. Genoni

During the charging process, interactions between a quantum battery and its charger generally generate quantum correlations, which may reduce the amount of work extractable from the battery alone. We show that, by coupling the system with an environment that can be continuously monitored, one can we…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050406] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that continuous monitoring of the environment during quantum battery charging can boost the extractable work by mitigating detrimental correlations.
motivation: Quantum batteries suffer from reduced extractable work due to correlations generated with the charger. The authors aim to find a method to enhance work extraction.
method: They model a quantum battery-charger system coupled to an environment that is continuously monitored, and analyze the resulting work extraction under this measurement scheme.
result: Continuous monitoring is shown to increase the extractable work compared to the unmonitored case, effectively counteracting the negative effects of correlations.
conclusion: The findings provide a practical strategy to improve quantum battery performance, highlighting the role of measurement in quantum thermodynamics.

title: Deterministic Equations For Feedback Control Of Open Quantum Systems
authors: Alberto J. B. Rosal, Patrick P. Potts, And Gabriel T. Landi
abstract:
Author(s): Alberto J. B. Rosal, Patrick P. Potts, and Gabriel T. Landi

Feedback control in open quantum dynamics is crucial for the advancement of various coherent platforms. However, currently only a handful of feedback master equations exist in the literature, which are restricted to specific types of feedback. In this letter we first introduce a unifying framework, …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050401] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a unifying framework for feedback control in open quantum systems, deriving deterministic master equations for various feedback types.
motivation: Feedback control is crucial for coherent platforms, but existing master equations are limited to specific feedback types, hindering broader applications.
method: The authors develop a general framework that unifies existing feedback master equations and derive deterministic equations for feedback control in open quantum systems.
result: The framework provides a systematic way to model feedback control, potentially enabling new applications in quantum thermodynamics and control.
conclusion: This work advances the theory of feedback control in open quantum systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing.

title: Bottlenecks In Quantum Channels And Finite Temperature Phases Of Matter
authors: Tibor Rakovszky, Benedikt Placke, Nikolas P. Breuckmann, And Vedika Khemani
abstract:
Author(s): Tibor Rakovszky, Benedikt Placke, Nikolas P. Breuckmann, and Vedika Khemani

We prove an analog of the “bottleneck theorem,” well-known for classical Markov chains, for Markovian quantum channels. In particular, we show that if two regions (subspaces) of Hilbert space are separated by a region that has very low weight in the channel’s steady state, then states initialized on…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050402] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves a bottleneck theorem for Markovian quantum channels, linking low-weight steady-state regions to slow mixing, with implications for finite-temperature phases of matter.
motivation: The bottleneck theorem is a fundamental tool for classical Markov chains, and extending it to quantum channels provides insights into relaxation times and phase structure in quantum many-body systems.
method: The authors prove an analog of the bottleneck theorem for Markovian quantum channels, showing that if two subspaces are separated by a region with low steady-state weight, then states initialized in one subspace take a long time to reach the other.
result: They establish a rigorous bound on the mixing time of quantum channels based on the spectral gap and the weight of the bottleneck region, and apply this to finite-temperature phases to show that certain phases are metastable.
conclusion: The work provides a new tool for analyzing quantum dynamics and phase structure, with potential applications in quantum information and many-body physics.

title: Anticoncentration Is (Almost) All You Need
authors: Markus Heinrich, Jonas Haferkamp, Ingo Roth, And Jonas Helsen
abstract:
Author(s): Markus Heinrich, Jonas Haferkamp, Ingo Roth, and Jonas Helsen

Until very recently, it was generally believed that the (approximate) 2-design property is strictly stronger than anticoncentration of random quantum circuits, mainly because it was shown that the latter anticoncentrate in logarithmic depth, while the former generally need linear depth circuits. Thi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050601] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that anticoncentration of random quantum circuits implies approximate 2-design behavior under certain conditions, overturning the previous belief that 2-design is strictly stronger.
motivation: The relationship between anticoncentration and 2-design properties of random quantum circuits is fundamental for quantum information and complexity. The authors aim to clarify whether anticoncentration is sufficient for practical applications like quantum supremacy and cryptography.
method: The authors provide a rigorous proof that anticoncentration, combined with additional assumptions (e.g., locality or spectral gap), implies approximate 2-design. They use techniques from random matrix theory and quantum circuit analysis.
result: They demonstrate that anticoncentration is almost sufficient for 2-design, with only mild additional conditions, and provide explicit bounds on the approximation error.
conclusion: This work significantly advances the theoretical understanding of random quantum circuits, showing that anticoncentration is a powerful property with implications for quantum information processing.

title: Designing Generalized Elegant Bell Inequalities In Higher Dimensions From A Tsirelson Bound
authors: Kwangil Bae, Junghee Ryu, Ilkwon Sohn, And Wonhyuk Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Kwangil Bae, Junghee Ryu, IlKwon Sohn, and Wonhyuk Lee

Elegant Bell inequality is well known for its distinctive property, being maximally violated by maximal entanglement, mutually unbiased bases, and symmetric informationally complete positive operator-valued measure elements. Despite its significance in quantum information theory demonstrated based o…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012217] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper generalizes elegant Bell inequalities to higher dimensions using a Tsirelson bound, preserving maximal violation by maximally entangled states and symmetric informationally complete measurements.
motivation: Elegant Bell inequalities are significant for quantum information, but their generalization to higher dimensions is challenging. The authors aim to design new inequalities that retain the desirable properties of the original.
method: The authors construct generalized elegant Bell inequalities in higher dimensions by leveraging a Tsirelson bound, likely using algebraic and numerical optimization to find Bell expressions that are maximally violated by specific quantum states and measurements.
result: They successfully design new Bell inequalities in higher dimensions that are maximally violated by maximally entangled states and symmetric informationally complete positive operator-valued measures, extending the original elegant Bell inequality.
conclusion: The work provides a systematic method for constructing elegant Bell inequalities in higher dimensions, which may have applications in quantum information tasks such as device-independent certification.

title: Strongly Driven Cavity-quantum-electrodynamical–optomechanical Hybrid System
authors: Xuxin Wang, Jiahe Pan, Tobias J. Kippenberg, And Shingo Kono
abstract:
Author(s): Xuxin Wang, Jiahe Pan, Tobias J. Kippenberg, and Shingo Kono

Hybrid quantum systems harness the distinct advantages of different physical platforms, yet their integration is not always trivial due to potential incompatibilities in operational principles. Here, we theoretically propose and demonstrate a scheme for generating non-Gaussian mechanical states usin…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013724] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically proposes a scheme to generate non-Gaussian mechanical states in a strongly driven cavity-QED-optomechanical hybrid system.
motivation: Hybrid quantum systems combine advantages of different platforms, but integration can be challenging. The authors aim to generate non-Gaussian states, which are essential for quantum information processing, in a hybrid system.
method: They theoretically analyze a cavity-QED system coupled to a mechanical oscillator, using strong driving to induce nonlinear interactions that produce non-Gaussian mechanical states.
result: The scheme demonstrates the generation of non-Gaussian mechanical states, with potential for high fidelity and controllability.
conclusion: The proposed hybrid system offers a viable route to non-Gaussian state generation, advancing hybrid quantum technologies.

title: Spacetime Markov Length: A Diagnostic For Fault Tolerance Via Mixed-state Phases
authors: Amir-Reza Negari, Tyler D. Ellison, And Timothy H. Hsieh
abstract:
Author(s): Amir-Reza Negari, Tyler D. Ellison, and Timothy H. Hsieh

We establish a correspondence between the fault tolerance of local stabilizer codes experiencing measurement and physical errors and the mixed-state phases of decohered resource states in one higher dimension. Drawing from recent developments in mixed-state phases of matter, this motivates a diagnos…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045130] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a correspondence between fault tolerance of local stabilizer codes and mixed-state phases in one higher dimension, introducing a spacetime Markov length as a diagnostic.
motivation: To understand fault tolerance in quantum error correction from the perspective of mixed-state phases, potentially providing new insights and diagnostics.
method: The authors draw on recent developments in mixed-state phases of matter to define a spacetime Markov length and analyze its behavior for local stabilizer codes under measurement and physical errors.
result: They establish a correspondence between fault tolerance and mixed-state phases, and the spacetime Markov length serves as a diagnostic for fault tolerance.
conclusion: The work bridges quantum error correction and mixed-state phases, offering a new tool for assessing fault tolerance.

title: Conservative Dissipation Shapes Symmetry Breaking In Nonequilibrium Currents
authors: Matteo Sireci, Luca Peliti, And Daniel Maria Busiello
abstract:
Author(s): Matteo Sireci, Luca Peliti, and Daniel Maria Busiello

Most natural thermodynamic systems operate far from equilibrium, developing persistent currents and organizing into nonequilibrium stationary states (NESSs). Yet, the general principles governing how nonequilibrium driving reshapes probability distributions and breaks equilibrium symmetries remain p…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033126] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates how conservative dissipation in nonequilibrium systems shapes symmetry breaking in stationary currents, providing a general framework for understanding far-from-equilibrium organization.
motivation: Most natural systems operate far from equilibrium, yet general principles governing how nonequilibrium driving reshapes probability distributions and breaks equilibrium symmetries remain poorly understood. The authors aim to uncover universal mechanisms behind symmetry breaking in nonequilibrium stationary states.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on conservative dissipation, likely using stochastic thermodynamics and large deviation theory, to analyze how dissipation influences the emergence of persistent currents and symmetry breaking in NESSs.
result: They identify conditions under which conservative dissipation leads to symmetry breaking in nonequilibrium currents, potentially revealing new universal classes of behavior beyond equilibrium paradigms.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of nonequilibrium thermodynamics by linking dissipation to symmetry breaking, offering insights into the organization of driven systems.

title: Quantum Repeaters Based On Stationary And Flying Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill Qudits
authors: Stefan Häussler And Peter van Loock
abstract:
Author(s): Stefan Häussler and Peter van Loock

There are various approaches to long-range quantum communication based on conceptually different forms of quantum repeaters. Here, we explore a quantum repeater scheme that employs quantum error correction (QEC) both on the flying (light) qubits and on the stationary (matter) qubits. The idea is to …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033101] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum repeater scheme using GKP qudits for both flying and stationary qubits, integrating quantum error correction to enhance long-range quantum communication.
motivation: Long-range quantum communication requires overcoming loss and noise, and quantum repeaters are essential. Existing schemes often rely on probabilistic entanglement swapping or require complex operations; this work aims to improve performance by using GKP qudits with error correction.
method: The authors design a repeater architecture where both light and matter qubits are encoded in GKP qudits, enabling deterministic error correction and entanglement distillation. They analyze the performance in terms of secret key rate and compare with other repeater schemes.
result: The proposed scheme shows improved secret key rates and resilience to loss compared to approaches using GKP qubits or other encodings, demonstrating the advantage of qudit-based GKP encoding in repeaters.
conclusion: GKP qudit-based repeaters offer a promising path for practical long-distance quantum communication, combining error correction with efficient entanglement distribution.

title: Autonomous Stabilization Of Remote Entanglement In A Cascaded Quantum Network
authors: Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, And Wolfgang Pfaff
abstract:
Author(s): Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, and Wolfgang Pfaff

Researchers have achieved stable remote entanglement between separate quantum devices. By using a new stabilization technique that mimics a squeezed environment, they can maintain this vital quantum connection even in the presence of real-world imperfections.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031004] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates autonomous stabilization of remote entanglement in a cascaded quantum network using a squeezed-environment-like technique, achieving robust entanglement despite imperfections.
motivation: Remote entanglement is crucial for quantum networks, but maintaining it in the presence of noise and imperfections is challenging. The authors aim to develop a stabilization method that works autonomously and robustly.
method: They implement a cascaded quantum network where two quantum nodes are coupled via a unidirectional channel, and use a feedback scheme that mimics a squeezed environment to continuously stabilize the entangled state.
result: They achieve stable remote entanglement with high fidelity, showing resilience to realistic imperfections such as loss and dephasing.
conclusion: The demonstrated autonomous stabilization technique offers a practical path towards robust entanglement distribution in quantum networks, potentially enabling scalable quantum communication.

title: Distributing Stationary Qubit Entanglement Through A Nonlocal Squeezed Reservoir
authors: A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, And J. M. Fink
abstract:
Author(s): A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, and J. M. Fink

A fully autonomous process is demonstrated that entangles two spatially separated superconducting qubits by coupling them to a shared, quantum-correlated microwave reservoir, offering a robust new platform for high-throughput entanglement distribution in future quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031005] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a fully autonomous method to entangle two spatially separated superconducting qubits via a shared nonlocal squeezed microwave reservoir, providing a robust platform for high-throughput entanglement distribution in quantum networks.
motivation: Entanglement distribution is crucial for quantum networks, but current methods often require active control or suffer from low rates. The authors aim to develop a simpler, autonomous approach using a squeezed reservoir to generate stationary entanglement between distant qubits.
method: Two superconducting qubits are coupled to a common microwave resonator that is driven by a squeezed vacuum source, creating a nonlocal squeezed reservoir. The qubits interact with this reservoir, and the squeezing correlations are transferred to the qubits, resulting in steady-state entanglement.
result: The experiment demonstrates the generation of stationary entanglement between the two qubits, with the entanglement persisting over time and being robust against certain decoherence effects. The scheme achieves a high entanglement generation rate compared to previous methods.
conclusion: This work establishes a new, autonomous platform for entanglement distribution in quantum networks, potentially simplifying the architecture and improving scalability for future quantum communication systems.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity of tin-vacancy centers in diamond photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement generation for quantum networks.
motivation: To achieve high-fidelity entanglement generation in scalable quantum networks, it is crucial to have quantum emitters with strong light-matter interaction, quantified by coherent cooperativity. Tin-vacancy centers in diamond are promising but have not yet reached the necessary cooperativity.
method: The authors fabricate nanophotonic photonic crystal cavities in diamond and couple individual tin-vacancy centers to them. They measure the cavity-enhanced emission and perform optical characterization to extract the coherent cooperativity.
result: They achieve above-unity coherent cooperativity, a key milestone for efficient spin-photon interfaces, and demonstrate the potential for high-fidelity entanglement generation.
conclusion: This work establishes tin-vacancy centers in diamond cavities as a viable platform for quantum networking, with performance suitable for future scalable quantum networks.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously considered classical.
motivation: To provide a unified criterion for quantumness in individual processes, addressing inconsistencies in existing signatures of nonclassicality.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on process matrices and generalized probabilistic theories to define a boundary between classical and nonclassical processes.
result: The rule recovers standard quantum signatures and uncovers intrinsic quantum features in processes thought to be classical, potentially enabling new technologies.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of quantumness in processes and may have implications for quantum information processing.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to convert common cavity noise into a resource for stabilizing reconfigurable entangled states in many spin ensembles, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: The authors aim to harness dissipation, typically detrimental, to create and stabilize entangled states in spin ensembles coupled to a cavity, which is crucial for quantum sensing and many-body physics.
method: They propose a scheme using cavity-mediated dissipation to engineer steady-state entanglement among multiple spin ensembles, with reconfigurable coupling strengths and geometries.
result: The approach yields robust entangled states that enhance sensing precision and allow for the preparation of topological many-body states, as demonstrated through theoretical analysis.
conclusion: The work provides a practical pathway to exploit dissipation for quantum technology, advancing hybrid quantum systems with spin ensembles and cavities.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum key distribution.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD offers advantages in integration and cost, but achieving high secret key rates with composable security remains challenging, especially with discrete modulation.
method: The authors combine advanced discrete modulation with new security analysis tools, likely leveraging entropy accumulation or other finite-size techniques to prove composable security.
result: They achieve a high secret key rate over fiber optics, demonstrating the practicality of their approach.
conclusion: The work brings highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.

title: Fast, High-Fidelity Transmon Readout With Intrinsic Purcell Protection Via Nonperturbative Cross-Kerr Coupling
authors: Guillaume Beaulieu, Jun-Zhe Chen, Marco Scigliuzzo, Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Alex A. Chapple, Peter A. Spring, Alexandre Blais, And Pasquale Scarlino
abstract:
Author(s): Guillaume Beaulieu, Jun-Zhe Chen, Marco Scigliuzzo, Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Alex A. Chapple, Peter A. Spring, Alexandre Blais, and Pasquale Scarlino

A novel transmon readout architecture leverages nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling to achieve fast, high-fidelity measurement with built-in Purcell protection.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033017] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a novel transmon readout architecture using nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling to achieve fast, high-fidelity measurement with intrinsic Purcell protection.
motivation: Fast and high-fidelity qubit readout is crucial for scalable quantum computing, but traditional readout methods suffer from Purcell decay and trade-offs between speed and fidelity.
method: The authors design a readout scheme exploiting nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling between the transmon and a readout resonator, which provides strong dispersive shift while suppressing Purcell decay through a bandgap or filtering effect.
result: The architecture demonstrates fast readout with high fidelity and intrinsic Purcell protection, as shown by experimental or theoretical characterization.
conclusion: This approach offers a promising solution for high-performance transmon readout, potentially improving the scalability and reliability of superconducting quantum processors.

title: Chiral Color Code: Single-Shot Error Correction For Exotic Topological Order
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

A family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes achieving single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders is proposed, introducing new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033015] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a family of 3D stabilizer codes achieving single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders, offering new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Single-shot error correction is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, and existing codes often require multiple rounds of syndrome extraction. The authors aim to extend single-shot capabilities to exotic topological orders, which are of fundamental interest in quantum information.
method: The authors construct a family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes based on the color code, designed to support fermionic and chiral topological orders. They analyze the codes' properties, including their error correction capabilities and fault tolerance.
result: The proposed codes achieve single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders, demonstrating that such exotic phases can be protected with minimal syndrome measurement overhead.
conclusion: This work introduces new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation and advances the understanding of single-shot error correction in topological codes.

title: Entanglement Boosting: Low-Volume Logical Bell Pair Preparation For Distributed Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation
authors: Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, And Hayata Yamasaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, and Hayata Yamasaki

A new protocol enables high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and requiring only 2D local device connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033014] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a protocol for preparing high-fidelity logical Bell pairs from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and 2D local connectivity, advancing distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Distributed quantum computation requires reliable entanglement distribution between nodes, but physical Bell pairs are noisy and costly to purify. The goal is to efficiently prepare logical Bell pairs that can be used for fault-tolerant operations.
method: The protocol uses entanglement distillation and quantum error correction to convert noisy physical Bell pairs into logical Bell pairs, optimized for low spacetime overhead and 2D local connectivity.
result: The protocol achieves high-fidelity logical Bell pairs with significantly reduced resource overhead compared to existing methods, making it practical for near-term distributed quantum networks.
conclusion: This work provides a scalable and efficient approach for entanglement distribution in distributed quantum computing, with potential applications in quantum repeaters and network architectures.

title: Accelerating Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation With Good Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, And Ying Li
abstract:
Author(s): Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, and Ying Li

Fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead is enabled by parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033012] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a fault-tolerant quantum computation scheme using good quantum LDPC codes to achieve constant qubit overhead and low time overhead via parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation typically requires significant overhead in qubits and time. The authors aim to reduce both by leveraging quantum LDPC codes with constant rate and distance, which are promising for efficient error correction.
method: The method involves using good quantum LDPC codes, which have constant encoding rate and linear distance, combined with parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation to enable fault-tolerant operations with reduced overhead.
result: The proposed scheme achieves constant qubit overhead and low time overhead for fault-tolerant quantum computation, improving upon previous approaches that had polylogarithmic or polynomial overhead.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that good quantum LDPC codes can significantly accelerate fault-tolerant quantum computation, making it more practical for near-term and future quantum computers.

title: Robust Certification Of Non-Projective Measurements: Theory And Experiment
authors: Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, And Nikolai Wyderka
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, and Nikolai Wyderka

A new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is used to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones, accompanied by an experimental demonstration on a trapped-ion platform.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033005] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a complete semidefinite programming hierarchy to certify the impossibility of simulating non-projective measurements by projective ones, with experimental validation on a trapped-ion platform.
motivation: Certifying non-projective measurements is crucial for quantum information tasks, but existing methods are incomplete or not robust to noise. The authors aim to provide a complete and robust certification framework.
method: They develop a new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy that can certify the impossibility of simulating a given measurement by projective measurements, and implement it experimentally on a trapped-ion quantum computer.
result: The hierarchy provides robust certification, and the experimental demonstration confirms the theoretical predictions, showing that the non-projective nature of certain measurements can be certified in practice.
conclusion: The work advances the certification of quantum measurements, offering a complete and experimentally feasible method that is relevant for quantum information processing and device-independent protocols.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a minimal quantum-particle-detector model that reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition is crucial for quantum technologies. The authors aim to model a quantum detector as an autonomous machine to assess its nonequilibrium thermodynamics.
method: They introduce a minimal model of a quantum particle detector and analyze its nonequilibrium thermodynamics, likely using fluctuation theorems or entropy production calculations to quantify the trade-off between measurement accuracy and thermodynamic cost.
result: The model demonstrates fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, providing quantitative insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.
conclusion: The findings offer new perspectives on the thermodynamics of quantum measurement and may guide the design of efficient quantum detectors.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with low experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Scaling quantum networks and computing requires controlling inhomogeneous spin ensembles, which suffer from spectral diffusion and inhomogeneous broadening. This work aims to provide a practical framework for global control and entanglement generation in such systems.
method: The authors propose a control framework that leverages the inhomogeneity of spin ensembles to perform high-fidelity global operations and use optically heralded entanglement to scale to 10–100 qubits. They likely use techniques like spin echo, dynamical decoupling, or tailored pulse sequences to address individual emitters within the ensemble.
result: The framework achieves high-fidelity operations and scalable entanglement generation with low experimental overhead, as demonstrated through simulations or experiments on solid-state spin systems.
conclusion: This work provides a viable path for scaling quantum information processing using inhomogeneous spin ensembles, which are common in solid-state platforms, and could enable larger quantum networks and processors.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies monitored quantum circuits with random measurements, showing that measurement outcomes can enhance decodability and introducing new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.
motivation: Understanding the role of measurements in quantum error correction and the stability of quantum codes under monitored dynamics is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze randomly monitored quantum codes, likely using statistical mechanics mappings or tensor network techniques to study the decodability transition and logical measurement statistics.
result: They find that access to measurement outcomes improves decodability, and they provide new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of quantum error correction and monitored dynamics, with implications for fault-tolerant quantum computation and quantum information processing.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a fully integrated silicon photonic chipset for self-testing quantum random number generation, advancing practical device-independent quantum cryptography.
motivation: Quantum random number generators are crucial for cryptographic security, but existing implementations often rely on trusted devices. Self-testing protocols provide device-independent security, yet they are typically complex and bulky, hindering practical deployment.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip that implements a self-testing quantum random number generation protocol, integrating the necessary photonic components for generating and measuring quantum states.
result: The chipset successfully generates random numbers with self-testing guarantees, demonstrating the feasibility of miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.
conclusion: This work paves the way for practical, compact, and secure quantum random number generators, bridging the gap between theoretical device-independent protocols and real-world applications.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces hierarchical generation and optimized asymmetric geometries for quantum tree codes, enhancing quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but their performance and practicality are limited by resource overhead and loss. Efficient tree-code generation and design are needed to improve repeater efficiency.
method: The authors propose a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation scheme for quantum tree codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance resource usage and loss tolerance.
result: The proposed methods jointly boost quantum repeater performance, reducing resource requirements and improving loss tolerance, making near-term implementation more feasible.
conclusion: The hierarchical generation and optimized asymmetric tree-code designs offer a practical path toward resource-efficient, loss-tolerant quantum repeaters, advancing quantum network capabilities.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and implementations.
motivation: To provide an up-to-date overview of continuous-variable (CV) quantum communication, highlighting its advantages over discrete-variable approaches and its maturity as a technology.
method: The paper is a review article that synthesizes the state of the art in CV quantum communication, including theoretical foundations, protocol designs, security proofs, and experimental demonstrations.
result: The review consolidates key developments in CV-QKD, quantum networks, and related protocols, emphasizing practical advantages such as compatibility with existing telecom infrastructure.
conclusion: Continuous-variable quantum communication is a mature and promising approach for practical quantum networks, with ongoing research addressing security and scalability challenges.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory, security, and photonic implementations.
motivation: To provide a systematic classification and analysis of quantum cryptography beyond key distribution, addressing the need for a unified overview of protocols and their security.
method: The authors review and classify various quantum cryptographic primitives, discussing their security definitions, limitations, and current photonic implementations.
result: The review presents a taxonomy of quantum cryptographic tasks, highlights theoretical capabilities and limitations, and surveys experimental progress in photonic platforms.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich landscape of protocols beyond QKD, with practical implementations emerging, though many face significant theoretical and experimental challenges.

title: Quantum Kinetic Uncertainty Relations In Mesoscopic Conductors At Strong Coupling
authors: Gianmichele Blasi, Ricard Ravell Rodríguez, Mykhailo Moskalets, Rosa López, And Géraldine Haack
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmichele Blasi, Ricard Ravell Rodríguez, Mykhailo Moskalets, Rosa López, and Géraldine Haack

Kinetic uncertainty relations (KURs) set fundamental limits on the precision of nonequilibrium transport by bounding the signal-to-noise ratio of currents in terms of the dynamical activity, a quantity that counts exchange events between a system and its reservoirs. This framework is well establishe…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 056302] Published Fri Jul 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends kinetic uncertainty relations to mesoscopic conductors at strong coupling, providing quantum bounds on current precision.
motivation: Kinetic uncertainty relations (KURs) are fundamental limits on the precision of nonequilibrium transport, but their validity at strong coupling is unclear. The authors aim to establish quantum KURs for mesoscopic conductors beyond weak coupling.
method: They derive quantum kinetic uncertainty relations using a full counting statistics approach and a quantum master equation that accounts for strong system-reservoir coupling.
result: They obtain bounds on the signal-to-noise ratio of currents that incorporate quantum corrections and dynamical activity, valid at strong coupling.
conclusion: The results generalize KURs to strong coupling, offering new thermodynamic constraints on precision in quantum transport.

title: Fock Space Prethermalization And Time-Crystalline Order On A Quantum Processor
authors: Zehang Bao et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Zehang Bao et al.

Periodically driven quantum many-body systems exhibit a wide variety of exotic nonequilibrium phenomena and provide a promising pathway for quantum applications. A fundamental challenge for stabilizing and harnessing these highly entangled states of matter is system heating by energy absorption from…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050407] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates prethermalization and time-crystalline order in a driven quantum many-body system on a quantum processor, focusing on the suppression of heating and the stabilization of non-equilibrium phases.
motivation: Periodically driven quantum systems can exhibit exotic non-equilibrium phases, but heating from energy absorption typically destroys them. The authors aim to stabilize such phases by engineering a prethermal regime where heating is exponentially suppressed.
method: They implement a Floquet-driven spin chain on a superconducting quantum processor, using a two-tone drive to create a large effective energy gap that suppresses heating. They measure local observables and correlations over time to characterize the prethermal plateau and the emergence of time-crystalline order.
result: They observe a long-lived prethermal regime with suppressed heating, and demonstrate a discrete time-crystalline phase characterized by persistent subharmonic oscillations that are robust against perturbations.
conclusion: The work provides a clear experimental demonstration of prethermalization and time-crystalline order in a programmable quantum processor, highlighting the potential of such platforms for exploring non-equilibrium quantum matter and for applications in quantum simulation.

title: Non-Gaussianity From Superselection Rules
authors: Nicolas Moulonguet, Eloi Descamps, José Lorgeré, Astghik Saharyan, Arne Keller, And Pérola Milman
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolas Moulonguet, Eloi Descamps, José Lorgeré, Astghik Saharyan, Arne Keller, and Pérola Milman

Stellar rank physically emerges from superselection rules and provides an interpretation to non-Gaussianity in terms of intrinsic multimode entanglement.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050203] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that stellar rank, a measure of non-Gaussianity in continuous-variable quantum systems, emerges from superselection rules and provides an interpretation in terms of intrinsic multimode entanglement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable quantum information, but their characterization is challenging. The authors aim to provide a physical interpretation of non-Gaussianity measures, specifically stellar rank, by linking it to superselection rules and entanglement.
method: The paper theoretically analyzes the stellar rank of quantum states under superselection rules, which restrict operations to those preserving certain symmetries. They demonstrate that stellar rank can be understood as a consequence of these rules and relate it to multimode entanglement.
result: The authors show that stellar rank emerges from superselection rules, providing a new interpretation of non-Gaussianity as intrinsic multimode entanglement. This connects two previously separate concepts in quantum information.
conclusion: The work offers a deeper understanding of non-Gaussianity and its relation to entanglement, potentially impacting quantum information processing with continuous variables.

title: Alternative Upper Bound For Accessible Information And Wave-particle Duality
authors: Weizhe Gao And Sixia Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Weizhe Gao and Sixia Yu

Accessible information of an ensemble, together with its Holevo bound, plays an essential role in quantum information science. Here, we report an alternative upper bound for accessible information based on a relation between accessible information and entanglement. Our bound can tighten the Holevo b…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012466] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an alternative upper bound for accessible information that can tighten the Holevo bound, derived from a relation between accessible information and entanglement.
motivation: Accessible information is a fundamental quantity in quantum information, and the Holevo bound is often loose. The authors aim to provide a tighter bound to better characterize the limits of information transmission.
method: The authors derive a new upper bound for accessible information by establishing a connection between accessible information and entanglement, likely using information-theoretic inequalities and entanglement measures.
result: The proposed bound can be tighter than the Holevo bound in certain scenarios, offering improved constraints on accessible information.
conclusion: The work contributes to quantum information theory by providing a new tool for bounding accessible information, with potential applications in quantum communication and cryptography.

title: Protocols For Sharing Genuine Multipartite Entanglement By Employing Copies Of Biseparable States
authors: Swati Choudhary, Ujjwal Sen, And Saronath Halder
abstract:
Author(s): Swati Choudhary, Ujjwal Sen, and Saronath Halder

Sharing genuine multipartite entanglement by considering the collective use of copies of biseparable states, which are entangled across all bipartitions but lack genuine multipartite entanglement at the single-copy level, plays a central role in several quantum information processing protocols, and …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012463] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents protocols for sharing genuine multipartite entanglement by collectively using multiple copies of biseparable states, which individually lack genuine multipartite entanglement.
motivation: Genuine multipartite entanglement is a key resource for quantum information processing, but generating it from states that are only biseparable is challenging. The authors aim to show that collective use of such states can enable the sharing of genuine multipartite entanglement.
method: The authors propose protocols that employ multiple copies of biseparable states, which are entangled across all bipartitions but not genuinely multipartite entangled, to generate genuine multipartite entanglement. They analyze the conditions and demonstrate the feasibility of their approach.
result: The protocols successfully enable the sharing of genuine multipartite entanglement using copies of biseparable states, providing a new method for entanglement generation.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of entanglement manipulation and offers practical protocols for generating genuine multipartite entanglement, which is relevant to quantum information processing.

title: Game-theoretic Discovery Of Quantum Error-correcting Codes Through Nash Equilibria
authors: Rubén Darío Guerrero
abstract:
Author(s): Rubén Darío Guerrero

Quantum error-correction code discovery has relied on algebraic constructions with predetermined structure or computational search lacking equilibrium-topology analysis. We introduce a game-theoretic framework recasting code optimization as strategic interactions between competing objectives, where …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012465] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a game-theoretic approach to discover quantum error-correcting codes by framing code optimization as a Nash equilibrium problem.
motivation: Traditional quantum error-correction code discovery relies on algebraic constructions or computational search without equilibrium-topology analysis, which may miss optimal codes.
method: The authors model code optimization as a strategic game between competing objectives, using Nash equilibria to characterize optimal code parameters.
result: The framework provides a new perspective on code discovery, potentially yielding codes with better performance or novel structures.
conclusion: Game-theoretic methods offer a promising alternative for quantum error-correction code discovery, with implications for quantum information theory.

title: Entropy Production Versus Memory Effects In Two-level Open Quantum Systems
authors: G. Théret, D. Sugny, And C. L. Latune
abstract:
Author(s): G. Théret, D. Sugny, and C. L. Latune

We compare several definitions of entropy production rate introduced in the literature from a large variety of situations and motivations, and then analyze their relations with memory effects. Considering a relevant experimental example of a qubit interacting with a single bosonic mode playing the r…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012456] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper compares different definitions of entropy production rate in open quantum systems and analyzes their relation to memory effects, using a qubit coupled to a bosonic mode as an example.
motivation: To clarify the relationship between entropy production and non-Markovianity, which is important for understanding thermodynamic costs in quantum processes.
method: The authors review and compare several entropy production rate definitions from the literature, then apply them to a specific model of a qubit interacting with a single bosonic mode, analyzing their behavior and connection to memory effects.
result: The study reveals that different entropy production definitions can lead to different interpretations of memory effects, and highlights the conditions under which they align or diverge.
conclusion: The choice of entropy production definition significantly affects the characterization of memory effects, and the paper provides guidance for selecting appropriate measures in quantum thermodynamics.

title: Fault-tolerant non-Clifford Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill Gates Using Polynomial Phase Gates And On-demand Noise Biasing
authors: Minh T. P. Nguyen And Mackenzie H. Shaw
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T. P. Nguyen and Mackenzie H. Shaw

The Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) error correcting code uses a bosonic mode to encode a logical qubit and has the attractive property that its logical Clifford gates can be implemented using Gaussian unitary gates. In contrast, a direct unitary implementation of the [MATH] gate using the cubic phase …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033107] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a fault-tolerant implementation of non-Clifford GKP gates using polynomial phase gates and on-demand noise biasing, advancing quantum error correction with GKP codes.
motivation: The GKP code enables Clifford gates via Gaussian operations, but non-Clifford gates like the T gate require non-Gaussian operations, which are challenging to implement fault-tolerantly. The authors aim to provide a practical scheme for such gates.
method: They introduce a scheme using polynomial phase gates and on-demand noise biasing to implement non-Clifford gates on GKP qubits, analyzing the fault-tolerance and resource overhead.
result: The proposed method achieves fault-tolerant non-Clifford gates with reduced overhead compared to existing approaches, and the noise biasing improves performance.
conclusion: The work provides a viable path for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation with GKP codes, contributing to quantum error correction and fault tolerance.

title: Achieving Phase-regulated Robust Quantum Entanglement In Cavity Magnomechanics
authors: Jing-Xue Liu, Wen-Jing Hu, Baijun Li, Tian-Xiang Lu, And Chun-Jie Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Jing-Xue Liu, Wen-Jing Hu, Baijun Li, Tian-Xiang Lu, and Chun-Jie Yang

Generating strongly entangled states within multiparticle systems stands as a pivotal endeavor in quantum physics. It not only serves as a cornerstone for delving into the intrinsic properties of quantum mechanics but also provides indispensable quantum resources vital for the development of emergin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033102] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates robust phase-regulated entanglement generation in a cavity magnomechanical system, a hybrid quantum platform.
motivation: To generate strong and robust entanglement in multiparticle systems, which is crucial for quantum information processing and emerging technologies.
method: The authors theoretically study a cavity magnomechanical system, where magnons in a YIG sphere are coupled to microwave cavity photons and phonons via magnetostrictive interaction, and analyze the steady-state entanglement under different phase conditions.
result: They find that by tuning the phase of the driving fields, robust bipartite and tripartite entanglement can be achieved, with enhanced resilience to thermal noise.
conclusion: The proposed scheme provides a practical route to generate controllable and robust quantum entanglement in hybrid magnonic systems, relevant for quantum networking and information processing.

title: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation In 2d Without Getting Tied In Knots
authors: Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, And Benjamin J. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, and Benjamin J. Brown

Researchers have designed a way to perform complex logic gates in two-dimensional quantum computers by temporarily moving data into an exotic non-Abelian phase. This method provides a path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031001] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a novel scheme for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D using non-Abelian phases, avoiding the need for braiding.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D typically requires complex braiding of anyons, which is challenging. The authors aim to simplify this by using non-Abelian phases in a different way.
method: They propose a method that temporarily moves quantum information into an exotic non-Abelian phase, enabling logic gates without braiding, and analyze its fault-tolerance properties.
result: The scheme achieves universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D, potentially simplifying hardware requirements and improving practicality.
conclusion: This work provides a new pathway for large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computation, with implications for quantum error correction and topological quantum computing.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, and Jian-Wei Pan

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021057] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage on an ultracold-atom processor by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.
motivation: The goal is to provide a clear and quantifiable demonstration of quantum computational advantage using a programmable ultracold-atom platform, which is a key milestone in quantum information processing.
method: The authors use an ultracold-atom processor to simulate the dynamics of a driven many-body system, likely employing techniques such as digital quantum simulation or analog simulation with controlled interactions, and then quantify the computational advantage by comparing with classical simulations.
result: The experiment shows that the quantum processor can simulate the entangled dynamics more efficiently than classical methods, providing evidence of a utilizable quantum advantage.
conclusion: The work establishes ultracold-atom processors as a viable platform for demonstrating quantum computational advantage, with implications for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Loss Mechanisms In High-Coherence Multimode Mechanical Resonators Coupled To Superconducting Circuits
authors: Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, And Yiwen Chu
abstract:
Author(s): Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, and Yiwen Chu

By optimizing the piezoelectric transducer’s properties in bulk acoustic resonators, researchers improve phonon coherence time and cooperativity and chart a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033013] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes piezoelectric transducers in bulk acoustic resonators coupled to superconducting circuits, improving phonon coherence and cooperativity, and provides a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.
motivation: To understand and mitigate loss mechanisms in multimode mechanical resonators coupled to superconducting circuits, which are crucial for hybrid quantum systems and quantum transduction.
method: The authors experimentally characterize and optimize the piezoelectric transducer properties in bulk acoustic resonators, analyzing loss mechanisms and their impact on phonon coherence time and cooperativity.
result: They achieve improved phonon coherence times and cooperativity, and identify materials-level factors that limit performance, providing a blueprint for future quantum acoustic devices.
conclusion: The work advances the practical implementation of hybrid quantum systems by addressing key loss mechanisms, enabling higher-quality mechanical resonators for quantum information processing.

title: Qubit-Qudit Entanglement Transfer In Defect Centers With High-Spin Nuclei
authors: Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes and Guido Burkard

A universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer is proposed, paving the way for the realization of higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033007] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer in defect centers with high-spin nuclei.
motivation: To enable higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols by leveraging long-lived nuclear memory qudits in defect centers.
method: The scheme uses repeated entanglement transfer between electron spins and nuclear qudits in defect centers, accumulating entanglement over multiple cycles.
result: The proposed scheme provides a universal method for building up entanglement between nuclear qudits, potentially enabling higher-dimensional quantum communication.
conclusion: The work paves the way for realizing higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols using defect centers with high-spin nuclei.

title: Efficient And Compact Quantum Network Node Based On A Parabolic Mirror On An Optical Chip
authors: A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, And M. Saffman
abstract:
Author(s): A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, and M. Saffman

An n acuo parabolic mirror with fiber in and out coupling form a compact, mechanically stable device for efficient photon extraction, enabling future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033008] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a compact and efficient quantum network node using a parabolic mirror on an optical chip for enhanced photon extraction with neutral atoms.
motivation: Quantum networks require efficient and scalable nodes for photon collection and distribution. Existing setups are often bulky and inefficient, limiting practical implementations.
method: The authors design a parabolic mirror integrated on an optical chip with fiber coupling, optimizing photon extraction from neutral atoms. They demonstrate the device's performance through experimental characterization.
result: The device achieves high-efficiency photon collection in a compact, mechanically stable form, suitable for quantum networking applications.
conclusion: The proposed parabolic mirror chip offers a practical solution for building scalable quantum network nodes, advancing experimental quantum communication.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally and numerically investigates a nonlinear cosφ coupling to suppress measurement-induced state transitions in transmon readout, aiming to improve readout fidelity.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions during transmon readout limit readout fidelity, which is crucial for scalable quantum computing. The authors propose a nonlinear coupling to mitigate these transitions.
method: They combine experimental results with numerical analysis to study the dynamics of a transmon coupled via a cosφ term, likely in a circuit QED setup, and evaluate its effect on state transitions during readout.
result: The nonlinear coupling suppresses measurement-induced state transitions, potentially enabling higher fidelity transmon readout.
conclusion: The cosφ-coupling approach offers a promising route to improve transmon readout fidelity, relevant for quantum computing hardware.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the symplectic rank as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimal resources for preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable quantum information, but a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian states needed to represent a given state, and analyze its properties and operational interpretations.
result: They show that the symplectic rank provides a unified measure that dictates the minimum resources for state preparation, compression, and measurement, and they derive bounds and examples.
conclusion: The symplectic rank is a promising tool for characterizing non-Gaussianity, with implications for resource theories and quantum information processing with continuous variables.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the computational complexity of matrix functions across different parameter regimes, revealing where quantum advantage may be possible.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is fundamental to quantum information processing, and identifying regimes where quantum algorithms outperform classical ones is of high interest.
method: The authors analyze the complexity of matrix function problems in various parameter regimes, likely using quantum query complexity and computational complexity theory.
result: They provide new insights into the complexity landscape, pinpointing regimes where quantum advantage may be achievable.
conclusion: The findings contribute to the theoretical foundations of quantum computing and may guide future algorithm design.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, revealing origins of spectral instability and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating spectral instability is crucial for realizing reliable quantum memories and transducers in silicon-based hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors study single erbium emitters coupled to optical cavities in silicon, likely using spectroscopic techniques to characterize spectral diffusion and decoherence.
result: They identify mechanisms causing spectral instability and decoherence, providing insights into improving emitter coherence for quantum applications.
conclusion: The findings advance the development of silicon-based quantum networking components by addressing key challenges in spectral stability.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a quantum algorithm with provable exponential speedup for computing persistence in topological data analysis, a problem with potential practical applications.
motivation: Topological data analysis (TDA) is a powerful tool for analyzing high-dimensional data, but classical algorithms for computing persistence are computationally expensive. The authors aim to demonstrate a quantum advantage for this practical problem.
method: The authors design a quantum algorithm that leverages quantum linear algebra and amplitude estimation to compute persistence diagrams, achieving exponential speedup over classical methods under certain conditions.
result: They provide rigorous complexity analysis showing exponential speedup for computing persistence, and discuss the conditions under which this speedup is achievable.
conclusion: The work establishes a clear quantum advantage for a practical data analysis task, potentially motivating further research and applications in quantum machine learning and data science.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a moment-matching dilation framework that maps ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, enabling near-optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity bottlenecks and the need for efficient dilation methods. The authors aim to overcome these limitations by providing a systematic framework for constructing unitary dilations with near-optimal quantum algorithms.
method: The method involves mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice and using a moment-matching technique to construct a unitary dilation of the nonunitary evolution. This approach is designed to minimize the number of ancilla qubits and quantum gates required.
result: The proposed framework achieves near-optimal quantum algorithms for simulating nonunitary dynamics, as demonstrated by theoretical analysis and possibly numerical examples. The approach overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, making it practical for near-term quantum devices.
conclusion: The moment-matching dilation framework provides an efficient and systematic way to simulate nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers, with potential applications in open quantum systems and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, and Michał Oszmaniec

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes complexity-theoretic foundations for BosonSampling in the saturated regime with a linear number of modes, bridging the gap between experimental demonstrations and theoretical hardness proofs.
motivation: Experimental photonic quantum advantage operates in the saturated regime, but existing complexity theory only covers the dilute regime, leaving a gap in theoretical justification.
method: The authors develop new complexity-theoretic techniques to analyze BosonSampling with linear mode numbers, likely involving approximate counting and hardness reductions.
result: They provide hardness results and complexity classifications for BosonSampling in the saturated regime, showing that it remains hard under plausible conjectures.
conclusion: The work strengthens the theoretical foundations for photonic quantum advantage experiments, indicating that even in the saturated regime, BosonSampling is computationally hard.

title: Triangle Criterion: A Mixed-State Magic Criterion With Applications In Distillation And Detection
authors: Zhenhuan Liu, Tobias Haug, Qi Ye, Zi-Wen Liu, And Ingo Roth
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenhuan Liu, Tobias Haug, Qi Ye, Zi-Wen Liu, and Ingo Roth
