Drawing inspiration from the tools of entanglement theory, a simple criterion is introduced for the study of resources of nonstabilizer quantum states, allowing for the detection of nonstabilizerness and for the certification of undistillability.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033016] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a simple criterion for detecting nonstabilizerness (magic) in mixed states and certifying undistillability, inspired by entanglement theory.
motivation: To provide a practical tool for detecting and quantifying magic in mixed states, which is crucial for quantum computing and resource theories.
method: The authors propose a 'triangle criterion' based on the convex hull of stabilizer states and use it to detect nonstabilizerness and certify undistillability.
result: The criterion enables detection of magic in mixed states and certification of undistillability, with applications in magic state distillation.
conclusion: The triangle criterion offers a simple and effective method for studying magic resources, advancing the resource theory of nonstabilizerness.

title: Fold-transversal Surface Code Cultivation
authors: Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, And Shruti Puri
abstract:
Author(s): Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (Katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, and Shruti Puri

A new strategy for magic-state cultivation achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033006] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a new magic-state cultivation strategy that reduces spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
motivation: Magic states are essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but their preparation is costly. Reducing the overhead of magic-state cultivation is crucial for practical quantum computers.
method: The authors propose a fold-transversal approach to surface code cultivation, leveraging nonlocal connectivity to improve efficiency.
result: The new strategy achieves lower spacetime overhead compared to existing methods, as demonstrated in the paper.
conclusion: The proposed cultivation strategy offers a more efficient path to magic states for quantum architectures with nonlocal connectivity, potentially advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Beam Search Decoder For Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Min Ye, Dave Wecker, And Nicolas Delfosse
abstract:
Author(s): Min Ye, Dave Wecker, and Nicolas Delfosse

A new decoding approach could achieve high accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction and avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033002] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a beam search decoder for quantum LDPC codes that achieves high decoding accuracy with low latency, suitable for real-time quantum error correction.
motivation: Quantum error correction requires efficient decoders that can operate in real-time, but existing decoders often trade off accuracy for speed or require massive classical resources.
method: The authors propose a beam search decoding algorithm that explores multiple candidate error patterns in parallel, balancing accuracy and computational cost.
result: The decoder demonstrates high accuracy and meets latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction, avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.
conclusion: The beam search decoder offers a practical solution for decoding quantum LDPC codes, potentially enabling real-time error correction in quantum computing systems.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020367] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a family of scalable planar fault-tolerant circuits for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code, achieving fault tolerance with a just-in-time decoder.
motivation: To enable universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings, which is a practical constraint for scalable quantum computers.
method: Designs twisted color circuits that implement non-Clifford gates fault-tolerantly on the 2D color code, and uses a just-in-time decoder to handle errors.
result: The proposed circuits are scalable and achieve fault tolerance, as demonstrated by the just-in-time decoder.
conclusion: The work provides a practical approach to fault-tolerant non-Clifford gates on planar architectures, advancing quantum error correction and fault tolerance.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive end-to-end quantum algorithm pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, demonstrating its use as a benchmark for quantum computers and exploring potential quantum advantage.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a powerful topological invariant with applications in knot theory and quantum gravity, but its approximation is classically hard. The authors aim to provide a practical quantum algorithm that can be implemented on near-term devices and serve as a benchmark for quantum advantage.
method: The authors develop a complete algorithmic pipeline, including state preparation, quantum phase estimation, and measurement, tailored for the Jones polynomial. They implement it on a trapped-ion quantum computer and analyze the resource requirements and error mitigation strategies.
result: They successfully demonstrate the algorithm on small instances, obtaining accurate approximations of the Jones polynomial for several knots. They also identify the computational bottlenecks and discuss the scalability and potential for quantum advantage.
conclusion: The work establishes a concrete quantum algorithm for a classically hard problem, providing a valuable benchmark for quantum hardware and a step towards demonstrating quantum advantage in a practical setting.

title: Experimental Realization Of Thermal Reservoirs With Tunable Temperature In A Trapped-Ion Spin-Boson Simulator
authors: Visal So, Mingjian Zhu, Midhuna Duraisamy Suganthi, Abhishek Menon, George Tomaras, Roman Zhuravel, Han Pu, And Guido Pagano
abstract:
Author(s): Visal So, Mingjian Zhu, Midhuna Duraisamy Suganthi, Abhishek Menon, George Tomaras, Roman Zhuravel, Han Pu, and Guido Pagano

We propose and demonstrate an experimental scheme to engineer thermal baths with independently tunable temperatures and dissipation rates for the motional modes of a trapped-ion system. This approach enables robust thermal-state preparation and quantum simulations of open-system dynamics in bosonic …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050604] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally demonstrates a trapped-ion simulator that engineers thermal reservoirs with tunable temperature and dissipation rates for bosonic modes, enabling quantum simulations of open-system dynamics.
motivation: The ability to simulate open quantum systems is crucial for understanding thermodynamics and decoherence, but experimental platforms with controllable thermal baths are limited. This work addresses the need for a versatile trapped-ion simulator to study quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors propose and implement a scheme using a trapped-ion system where the motional modes are coupled to engineered reservoirs with independently tunable temperatures and dissipation rates, achieved through controlled laser-induced interactions.
result: They successfully demonstrate robust thermal-state preparation and simulate open-system dynamics, showing the tunability of the engineered thermal baths.
conclusion: This trapped-ion platform provides a powerful tool for quantum simulations of open-system dynamics and quantum thermodynamics, with potential applications in studying heat engines and thermalization.

title: High-Temperature Limit Penalizing High-Frequency Quantum Fluctuations
authors: Graeme Pleasance, Erik Aurell, And Francesco Petruccione
abstract:
Author(s): Graeme Pleasance, Erik Aurell, and Francesco Petruccione

We revisit the Caldeira-Leggett model of quantum Brownian motion with Ohmic spectral density, and derive an additional contribution to the decoherence kernel in a new high-temperature limit at arbitrarily large cutoff frequency. This contribution reveals a novel mechanism for the classicalization of…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050405] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper revisits the Caldeira-Leggett model and finds a new high-temperature limit that penalizes high-frequency quantum fluctuations, revealing a novel classicalization mechanism.
motivation: To understand the quantum-to-classical transition in open quantum systems, specifically the role of high-frequency fluctuations in decoherence.
method: The authors derive an additional contribution to the decoherence kernel in the Caldeira-Leggett model under a high-temperature limit with arbitrarily large cutoff frequency.
result: They identify a new mechanism for classicalization that suppresses high-frequency quantum fluctuations, extending the standard decoherence picture.
conclusion: The work provides deeper insight into the thermodynamic and information-theoretic aspects of decoherence, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.

title: Kicked-Ising Quantum Battery
authors: Sebastián V. Romero, Xi Chen, And Yue Ban
abstract:
Author(s): Sebastián V. Romero, Xi Chen, and Yue Ban

Entanglement has been identified as a key resource for enhancing charging performance in quantum batteries. We show that the kicked-Ising model at the self-dual point provides an explicit charging mechanism, where maximal entanglement growth yields maximal energy injection. Identifying the Floquet d…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050404] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a kicked-Ising model as a quantum battery, showing that maximal entanglement growth leads to maximal energy injection.
motivation: Quantum batteries are a key topic in quantum thermodynamics, and entanglement is known to enhance charging performance. The authors aim to provide an explicit charging mechanism using a kicked-Ising model.
method: They analyze the kicked-Ising model at the self-dual point, using Floquet dynamics to study entanglement growth and energy injection.
result: They find that maximal entanglement growth corresponds to maximal energy injection, demonstrating an explicit connection between entanglement and battery charging.
conclusion: The kicked-Ising model serves as an effective quantum battery, and the results highlight the role of entanglement in optimizing energy storage.

title: Topological Robustness Of Orbital Angular Momentum Entanglement In Stochastic Channels
authors: Tatjana Kleine, Pedro Ornelas, Cade Peters, Zhenyu Guo, Bereneice Sephton, Isaac Nape, Yijie Shen, And Andrew Forbes
abstract:
Author(s): Tatjana Kleine, Pedro Ornelas, Cade Peters, Zhenyu Guo, Bereneice Sephton, Isaac Nape, Yijie Shen, and Andrew Forbes

Orbital angular momentum (OAM) entanglement gives access to multiple qubit and high dimensional Hilbert spaces but is unfortunately susceptible to disturbance, decaying in real-world noisy channels. Here, we show that an underlying topology arising from OAM entanglement remains robust to such channe…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050602] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that the topological structure of orbital angular momentum (OAM) entanglement remains robust in stochastic noisy channels, offering a new perspective on entanglement preservation.
motivation: OAM entanglement is promising for high-dimensional quantum information but is fragile in real-world noisy channels. The authors aim to find a property that survives such noise, potentially enabling more robust quantum communication.
method: They theoretically and experimentally investigate the topology of OAM entanglement, likely using skyrmionic or other topological invariants, and test its robustness under stochastic channel noise.
result: They find that the underlying topology of OAM entanglement is robust to stochastic disturbances, even when the entanglement itself degrades, suggesting a new resource for quantum information processing.
conclusion: The topological robustness of OAM entanglement could be exploited for noise-resilient quantum protocols, opening new avenues for high-dimensional quantum communication and information processing.

title: Observing Quantum Correlation Dynamics In Tunable Superconducting Bose-Hubbard Simulators
authors: Z. T. Wang, Si-Yun Zhou, Yun-Hao Shi, Kaixuan Huang, Z. H. Yang, Jingning Zhang, Kui Zhao, Yueshan Xu, Hao Li, S. K. Zhao, Yulong Feng, Guangming Xue, Yu Liu, Wei-Guo Ma, Cai-Ping Fang, Hao-Tian Liu, Yong-Yi Wang, Kai Xu, Haifeng Yu, Heng Fan, And S. P. Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Z. T. Wang, Si-Yun Zhou, Yun-Hao Shi, Kaixuan Huang, Z. H. Yang, Jingning Zhang, Kui Zhao, Yueshan Xu, Hao Li, S. K. Zhao, Yulong Feng, Guangming Xue, Yu Liu, Wei-Guo Ma, Cai-Ping Fang, Hao-Tian Liu, Yong-Yi Wang, Kai Xu, Haifeng Yu, Heng Fan, and S. P. Zhao

The dynamics of quantum correlations are central to understanding many physical properties of quantum systems. Here we experimentally study the correlation dynamics via two-particle quantum walks in superconducting Bose-Hubbard qutrit arrays, with tunable on-site interaction [MATH] realized by Floquet …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050603] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally studies quantum correlation dynamics via two-particle quantum walks in a tunable superconducting Bose-Hubbard simulator, demonstrating control over on-site interactions using Floquet engineering.
motivation: Understanding quantum correlation dynamics is fundamental to many-body physics and quantum simulation. The authors aim to experimentally realize a tunable Bose-Hubbard model with superconducting circuits to observe these dynamics.
method: They implement a superconducting Bose-Hubbard qutrit array with tunable on-site interaction via Floquet engineering, and perform two-particle quantum walks to probe correlation dynamics.
result: The experiment demonstrates the ability to tune interactions and observe distinct correlation dynamics, showing the versatility of superconducting simulators for studying quantum many-body phenomena.
conclusion: The work highlights superconducting circuits as a powerful platform for quantum simulation of Bose-Hubbard physics, with potential applications in quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Role Of Entanglement In Quantum Reservoir Computing With Coupled Kerr Nonlinear Oscillators
authors: Ali Karimi, Hadi Zadeh-Haghighi, Youssef Kora, And Christoph Simon
abstract:
Author(s): Ali Karimi, Hadi Zadeh-Haghighi, Youssef Kora, and Christoph Simon

Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) uses quantum dynamics to efficiently process temporal data. In this work, we investigate a QRC framework based on two coupled Kerr nonlinear oscillators, a system well suited for time-series prediction tasks due to its complex nonlinear interactions and potentially …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012468] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the role of entanglement in quantum reservoir computing using two coupled Kerr nonlinear oscillators, showing that entanglement enhances performance in time-series prediction tasks.
motivation: Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) is a promising approach for temporal data processing, but the role of entanglement in its performance is not well understood. Understanding this can guide the design of more efficient quantum reservoirs.
method: The authors implement a QRC framework based on two coupled Kerr nonlinear oscillators, which exhibit complex nonlinear dynamics. They systematically vary the coupling strength and measure the entanglement between the oscillators, then evaluate the reservoir's performance on time-series prediction tasks.
result: They find that the presence of entanglement correlates with improved prediction accuracy, and that optimal performance occurs in a regime with moderate entanglement, suggesting entanglement is a resource for QRC.
conclusion: Entanglement plays a beneficial role in quantum reservoir computing with coupled Kerr oscillators, and controlling entanglement can enhance computational capabilities.

title: Enhancing Long-distance Continuous-variable Quantum Key Distribution With An Error-correcting Relay
authors: S. Nibedita Swain, Ryan J. Marshman, Josephine Dias, Matthew S. Winnel, Alexander S. Solntsev, And Timothy C. Ralph
abstract:
Author(s): S. Nibedita Swain, Ryan J. Marshman, Josephine Dias, Matthew S. Winnel, Alexander S. Solntsev, and Timothy C. Ralph

Noiseless linear amplifiers serve as an effective means to enable long-distance continuous-variable (CV) quantum key distribution (QKD), even under realistic conditions with nonunit reconciliation efficiency. Separately, unitary averaging has been suggested to mitigate some stochastic noise, includi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012625] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an error-correcting relay using noiseless linear amplifiers and unitary averaging to enhance long-distance continuous-variable QKD.
motivation: Long-distance CV-QKD is limited by noise and loss; noiseless linear amplifiers can help but suffer from stochastic noise. The authors aim to improve performance under realistic conditions.
method: They combine noiseless linear amplification with unitary averaging to mitigate stochastic noise, and analyze the protocol's performance with nonunit reconciliation efficiency.
result: The proposed relay extends the achievable distance and improves key rates compared to standard approaches, even with realistic imperfections.
conclusion: The error-correcting relay offers a practical enhancement for long-distance CV-QKD, making it more viable for quantum network applications.

title: Deterministic Equations For Feedback Control Of Open Quantum Systems. Ii. Properties Of The Memory Function
authors: Alberto J. B. Rosal, Patrick P. Potts, And Gabriel T. Landi
abstract:
Author(s): Alberto J. B. Rosal, Patrick P. Potts, and Gabriel T. Landi

Feedback uses past detection outcomes to dynamically modify a quantum system and is central to quantum control. These outcomes can be stored in a memory, defined as a stochastic function of past measurements. In this work, we investigate the main properties of a general memory function subject to ar…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012215] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives deterministic equations for feedback control of open quantum systems, focusing on the properties of a memory function that stores past measurement outcomes.
motivation: Feedback control is essential for quantum technologies, and understanding how memory of past outcomes influences system dynamics is crucial for optimal control.
method: The authors develop a general framework for feedback control with a memory function, deriving deterministic equations of motion and analyzing the properties of the memory function.
result: They characterize the memory function's properties, such as its dependence on measurement outcomes and its role in the feedback dynamics, potentially leading to simplified control strategies.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for feedback control in open quantum systems, with implications for quantum control and thermodynamics.

title: Deterministic Equations For Feedback Control Of Open Quantum Systems. Iii. Full Counting Statistics For Jump-based Feedback
authors: Alberto J. B. Rosal, Guilherme Fiusa, Patrick P. Potts, And Gabriel T. Landi
abstract:
Author(s): Alberto J. B. Rosal, Guilherme Fiusa, Patrick P. Potts, and Gabriel T. Landi

In this work, we consider a general feedback protocol based on quantum-jump detections, where the last detected jump channel is stored in a memory and subsequently used to implement a feedback action, such as modifying the system Hamiltonian conditioned on the last jump. We show that the time evolut…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012216] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives deterministic equations for the full counting statistics of quantum-jump-based feedback control in open quantum systems, providing a general framework for analyzing feedback protocols.
motivation: Feedback control is crucial for quantum technologies, but existing methods often rely on stochastic master equations. The authors aim to provide a deterministic and efficient way to compute the statistics of jump-based feedback, which is important for characterizing and optimizing such protocols.
method: The authors develop a formalism based on the full counting statistics of quantum jumps, incorporating a memory of the last detected jump channel. They derive deterministic equations for the generating function and cumulants of the jump statistics, extending previous work on feedback control.
result: They obtain closed-form equations for the full counting statistics, which can be used to compute quantities like the average number of jumps and their fluctuations. The framework is general and applicable to a wide range of feedback protocols.
conclusion: The work provides a powerful tool for analyzing quantum feedback control, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing. It advances the theoretical understanding of feedback in open quantum systems.

title: Quantum Scrambling Born Machine
authors: Marcin Płodzień
abstract:
Author(s): Marcin Płodzień

We propose a quantum scrambling Born machine (QSBM) that decouples entanglement generation from the trainable degrees of freedom: a fixed, nontrainable scrambling unitary provides multiqubit entanglement while only single-qubit rotations are optimized. We consider three entangling unitaries (a Haar …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012464] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a quantum scrambling Born machine that uses a fixed scrambling unitary for entanglement and optimizes only single-qubit rotations, demonstrating efficient training for quantum state generation.
motivation: To address the challenge of training quantum circuits with many entangling gates by decoupling entanglement generation from trainable parameters, potentially improving trainability and resource efficiency.
method: The QSBM uses a fixed, non-trainable scrambling unitary (e.g., Haar random, Clifford, or hardware-efficient) to generate multiqubit entanglement, while only single-qubit rotations are optimized. The authors consider three types of entangling unitaries and train the model using a loss function based on fidelity or cross-entropy.
result: The QSBM achieves high fidelity in generating target quantum states, with performance depending on the choice of scrambling unitary. The approach reduces the number of trainable parameters and avoids barren plateaus, as demonstrated in numerical simulations.
conclusion: The QSBM provides a promising framework for quantum generative modeling, leveraging scrambling dynamics to simplify training while maintaining expressibility, with potential applications in quantum state preparation and quantum machine learning.

title: Full Schmidt Characterization Of Spatiotemporally Entangled States Produced From Spontaneous Parametric Down-conversion
authors: Rakesh Pradhan And Girish Kulkarni
abstract:
Author(s): Rakesh Pradhan and Girish Kulkarni

The full Schmidt decomposition of spatiotemporally entangled states generated from spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) has not been carried out until now due to the immense computational complexity arising from the large dimensionalities of the states. In this article, we utilize the rotat…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013722] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents the first full Schmidt decomposition of spatiotemporally entangled states from SPDC using a rotation-based method, providing a complete characterization of their entanglement structure.
motivation: The full Schmidt decomposition of SPDC states has been computationally intractable due to high dimensionality, limiting understanding of their entanglement properties. The authors aim to overcome this to enable better characterization and applications.
method: They employ a rotation-based approach to compute the Schmidt decomposition, efficiently handling the large Hilbert space dimensions of the spatiotemporal modes.
result: They obtain the full Schmidt decomposition, revealing the entanglement spectrum and mode structure of the SPDC states, which was previously unavailable.
conclusion: The work provides a complete entanglement characterization of SPDC states, which is fundamental for quantum information processing and may enable optimized protocols.

title: Phase-switchable Nonreciprocal Entanglement Via Magnon Squeezing In Ring-cavity Optomagnomechanics
authors: Z. Imara, A. El Allati, A. Belfakir, K. El Anouz, And I. Pérez Castillo
abstract:
Author(s): Z. Imara, A. El Allati, A. Belfakir, K. El Anouz, and I. Pérez Castillo

Cavity optomagnomechanics provides a versatile platform to explore macroscopic quantum correlations, particularly nonreciprocal entanglement. In this work we propose a theoretical scheme to generate switchable bipartite and tripartite entanglement in an optomagnomechanical ring cavity by exploiting …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012460] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a theoretical scheme to generate switchable bipartite and tripartite entanglement in an optomagnomechanical ring cavity using magnon squeezing.
motivation: To explore macroscopic quantum correlations, specifically nonreciprocal entanglement, in a cavity optomagnomechanical platform, which is relevant for quantum information processing and hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a ring-cavity optomagnomechanical system with magnon squeezing, deriving the quantum Langevin equations and calculating entanglement measures (e.g., logarithmic negativity) for bipartite and tripartite subsystems.
result: They demonstrate that by tuning the phase of the driving fields and magnon squeezing, the entanglement can be switched on/off and made nonreciprocal, showing controllable quantum correlations.
conclusion: The scheme provides a versatile platform for generating and controlling nonreciprocal entanglement, which could be useful for quantum networking and information processing applications.

title: Optimal Majoranas In Mesoscopic Kitaev Chains
authors: M. Alvarado, R. Seoane Souto, Maria José Calderón, And Ramón Aguado
abstract:
Author(s): M. Alvarado, R. Seoane Souto, Maria José Calderón, and Ramón Aguado

Kitaev chains realized in quantum dots coupled via superconducting segments provide a controllable platform for engineering Majorana zero modes (MZMs). In these systems, subgap states in the hybrid region mediate the effective coupling between quantum dots and determine the emergence of sweet spots …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034512] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies optimal conditions for Majorana zero modes in mesoscopic Kitaev chains realized with quantum dots and superconducting segments, focusing on sweet spots and subgap state effects.
motivation: To understand and optimize the emergence of Majorana zero modes in hybrid quantum dot-superconductor systems, which are promising for topological quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze a Kitaev chain model with quantum dots coupled via superconducting segments, considering subgap states in the hybrid region and their influence on the effective coupling and sweet spots.
result: They identify optimal parameter regimes for robust Majorana zero modes, showing how subgap states can be tuned to enhance the topological phase and improve the quality of the MZMs.
conclusion: The findings provide practical guidance for engineering mesoscopic Kitaev chains with improved Majorana properties, advancing the feasibility of topological qubits.

title: Nonreciprocal Dynamics With Weak Noise: Aperiodic “Escher Cycles” And Their Quasipotential Landscape
authors: Janik Schüttler, Robert L. Jack, And Michael E. Cates
abstract:
Author(s): Janik Schüttler, Robert L. Jack, and Michael E. Cates

Nonequilibrium systems with multiple metastable states can undergo noise-induced transitions that form cycles among the metastable states. To analyze this phenomenon, the authors introduce a minimal two-dimensional stochastic model with nonreciprocal couplings that can be treated analytically.

#TechnicalAdvancement #AdvancingField


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024104] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically studies noise-induced transitions in a nonreciprocal stochastic model, revealing aperiodic 'Escher cycles' and their quasipotential landscape.
motivation: To understand how nonreciprocal couplings in nonequilibrium systems lead to cyclic transitions among metastable states, which is a fundamental aspect of stochastic thermodynamics.
method: The authors introduce a minimal two-dimensional stochastic model with nonreciprocal couplings and treat it analytically, likely using path integral or large deviation techniques to derive the quasipotential.
result: They find that the system exhibits aperiodic cycles (Escher cycles) and characterize their quasipotential landscape, providing insights into the thermodynamics of such transitions.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of noise-induced transitions in nonreciprocal systems, with implications for nonequilibrium thermodynamics and stochastic dynamics.

title: Elementary Derivation Of The Dissipation-coherence Bound For Stochastic Oscillators
authors: Artemy Kolchinsky
abstract:
Author(s): Artemy Kolchinsky

The dissipation-coherence bound is a conjectured trade-off between entropy production and the quality of stochastic oscillations. We show that this bound can be derived by combining the higher-order “thermodynamic uncertainty relation” with a simple condition on phase-current fluctuations. In one-di…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L012104] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives the dissipation-coherence bound for stochastic oscillators by combining higher-order thermodynamic uncertainty relations with a condition on phase-current fluctuations.
motivation: The dissipation-coherence bound is a conjectured trade-off between entropy production and oscillation quality, and a rigorous derivation is needed.
method: The author combines the higher-order thermodynamic uncertainty relation with a simple condition on phase-current fluctuations to derive the bound.
result: The paper provides an elementary derivation of the dissipation-coherence bound, confirming the conjecture.
conclusion: The result strengthens the theoretical foundation for understanding thermodynamic costs in stochastic oscillators, relevant to information thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Speedup From Nonclassical Polarization
authors: Tim Aßbrock, Jan Sperling, And Laura Ares
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Aßbrock, Jan Sperling, and Laura Ares

Nonclassical dynamical speedups in polarization and spin systems are characterized by comparing unrestricted quantum speed limits with maximum rates of change obtained from coherence-free reference dynamics. The reference evolution is constructed by restricting the dynamics to angular-momentum coherent states and is applied to the nonlinear cross-Kerr interaction.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032018] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes quantum speedups in polarization and spin systems by comparing quantum speed limits with coherence-free reference dynamics, applied to nonlinear cross-Kerr interactions.
motivation: To identify and quantify the role of nonclassical coherence in enabling faster-than-classical dynamical evolution, which is a fundamental question in quantum thermodynamics and information processing.
method: The authors construct a reference evolution restricted to angular-momentum coherent states (coherence-free) and compare the maximum rate of change (quantum speed limit) of the full quantum dynamics with this reference, using the nonlinear cross-Kerr interaction as a testbed.
result: They demonstrate that nonclassical polarization (quantum coherence) can lead to a genuine speedup beyond what is achievable with coherence-free states, providing a quantitative measure of quantum advantage in dynamics.
conclusion: The work establishes a framework for identifying and quantifying quantum speedups due to nonclassical coherence, with implications for quantum control and thermodynamics.

title: Dynamical Tipping In A Quantum Limit Cycle
authors: Ya-Xin Xiang, Zhengyang Bai, And Yu-Qiang Ma
abstract:
Author(s): Ya-Xin Xiang, Zhengyang Bai, and Yu-Qiang Ma

Nonequilibrium systems maintain spatiotemporal order through energy dissipation and entropy production. Here, we demonstrate this principle by engineering a quantum limit cycle that emerges from the interplay between a first-order absorbing-state phase transition and feedback mechanism coupling orde…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033100] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a quantum limit cycle emerging from an absorbing-state phase transition and feedback, linking non-equilibrium dynamics to information thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how non-equilibrium systems maintain order through dissipation and feedback, and to explore quantum versions of limit cycles.
method: They engineer a quantum limit cycle by coupling an absorbing-state phase transition with a feedback mechanism, likely using a master equation or stochastic simulation.
result: They observe a stable limit cycle in the quantum regime, characterized by periodic oscillations in order parameter and entropy production.
conclusion: The work provides a concrete example of a quantum limit cycle, highlighting the role of feedback and phase transitions in non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics.

title: Mixed State Entanglement Via The Cauchy-Schwarz Inequality
authors: Nishaant Jacobus, Paul Brumer, And Chern Chuang
abstract:
Author(s): Nishaant Jacobus, Paul Brumer, and Chern Chuang

This work develops an approach to analyze the quantum entanglement of mixed states by comparing the relative magnitudes of populations and coherences of the density operator. This is applied to models of light-matter interaction to examine how the symmetries of the interaction influence entanglement in thermal and nonequilibrium steady states.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032014] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a method to analyze mixed-state entanglement by comparing populations and coherences, applied to light-matter interaction models.
motivation: To provide a practical approach for quantifying entanglement in mixed states, which is often challenging, and to understand how interaction symmetries affect entanglement in thermal and steady states.
method: The authors develop an entanglement criterion based on the relative magnitudes of populations and coherences in the density matrix, and apply it to models of light-matter interaction.
result: The method successfully identifies entanglement in thermal and nonequilibrium steady states, revealing the influence of interaction symmetries on entanglement.
conclusion: The proposed approach offers a useful tool for analyzing mixed-state entanglement, with implications for quantum information processing in open systems.

title: Engineering Magnon Lasing In Full Quantum Regime
authors: Yan Liu And Jiahua Li
abstract:
Author(s): Yan Liu and Jiahua Li

We develop an analytical approach for steady-state normal-ordered magnon moments (NOMMs) in a driven-dissipative magnon-qubit system with coherent and dissipative couplings, and further benchmark it against the full quantum master-equation simulations of mean magnon number and second-order intensity…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033088] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an analytical approach for steady-state magnon moments in a driven-dissipative magnon-qubit system, benchmarking it against full quantum master-equation simulations to engineer magnon lasing in the full quantum regime.
motivation: Understanding and controlling magnon lasing in hybrid quantum systems is important for quantum information processing and quantum thermodynamics applications.
method: The authors derive analytical expressions for steady-state normal-ordered magnon moments (NOMMs) in a system with coherent and dissipative couplings, and compare them with numerical simulations of the quantum master equation.
result: The analytical approach accurately predicts mean magnon number and second-order intensity correlations, demonstrating the feasibility of engineering magnon lasing in the full quantum regime.
conclusion: The work provides a useful theoretical tool for designing magnon-based quantum devices and contributes to the understanding of quantum nonlinear dynamics in hybrid systems.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using entangled Lieb-Mattis states for robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.
motivation: Quantum sensors are limited by noise and scalability; differential phase sensing is important for many applications, but existing entangled states are fragile to common-mode noise.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework for generating and using Lieb-Mattis states in atomic ensembles or spin systems, and analyze their sensitivity and robustness to noise.
result: They show that Lieb-Mattis states provide a practical advantage for differential phase sensing, with enhanced precision and intrinsic common-mode noise rejection.
conclusion: This work offers a promising route to scalable quantum sensor networks using entangled states that are robust to realistic noise.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems, enabling squeezed and higher-order squeezed states for quantum sensing and error correction.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are crucial for quantum technologies, but generating arbitrary superpositions is challenging. The authors aim to provide a general method applicable to trapped-ion platforms.
method: They use a trapped-ion system with a protocol that combines spin-dependent forces and engineered interactions to synthesize arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states, including squeezed and trisqueezed states.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, demonstrating the versatility of their approach.
conclusion: The method offers a powerful tool for generating non-classical states in trapped ions, with potential applications in quantum sensing and error correction.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates passive quantum error correction of photon loss at the breakeven point using continuous drives, extending a qubit's lifetime beyond its physical limits.
motivation: Active quantum error correction requires measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors. Passive schemes could simplify error correction and improve qubit lifetimes.
method: The authors implement a passive quantum error correction scheme using continuous drives in a superconducting circuit, likely a cavity or resonator coupled to a transmon qubit, to protect against photon loss without active measurements.
result: They achieve error correction at the breakeven point, meaning the corrected qubit lifetime exceeds the uncorrected physical lifetime, demonstrating a practical improvement.
conclusion: Passive error correction can be effective at breakeven, offering a simpler alternative to active schemes and potentially advancing quantum computing hardware.

title: On-Chip Levitated Neon Particle Arrays For Robust And Scalable Electron Qubits
authors: Sosuke Inui, Yinghe Qi, Yiming Xing, Charles Peretti, Dafei Jin, And Wei Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Sosuke Inui, Yinghe Qi, Yiming Xing, Charles Peretti, Dafei Jin, and Wei Guo

An on-chip magnetic levitation architecture for robust and highly tunable electron-on-neon qubits is proposed, identifying a potential pathway toward scalable quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033019] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an on-chip magnetic levitation architecture for electron-on-neon qubits, aiming for robust and scalable quantum computation.
motivation: Electron-on-neon qubits are a promising platform but face challenges in scalability and robustness; the authors aim to address these with a novel on-chip magnetic levitation design.
method: The authors propose a theoretical architecture using on-chip magnetic levitation to trap and control neon particle arrays, which host electron qubits, and analyze its feasibility and tunability.
result: The proposed architecture shows potential for robust and highly tunable qubits, offering a pathway toward scalable quantum computation.
conclusion: The work identifies a promising direction for scalable electron-on-neon qubits, though experimental realization remains to be demonstrated.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: To achieve optimal sensitivity in displacement sensing, which is crucial for quantum metrology and sensing applications.
method: The authors propose and analyze a scheme using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion systems, likely involving quantum control and measurement techniques.
result: They show that this approach enables optimal displacement sensing, surpassing standard quantum limits.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions provide a practical route to high-precision displacement sensing, with implications for quantum metrology.

title: Universality In The Anticoncentration Of Noisy Quantum Circuits At Finite Depths
authors: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo de Nardis, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo De Nardis, and Andrea De Luca

A universal description of noisy random circuits reveals depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent anticoncentration.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020365] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a universal description of anticoncentration in noisy random quantum circuits at finite depths, revealing depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent behavior.
motivation: Understanding anticoncentration in noisy quantum circuits is crucial for assessing the computational power of near-term quantum devices and for benchmarking quantum advantage experiments.
method: The authors analyze the anticoncentration properties of random circuits under depolarizing noise, using techniques from random matrix theory and statistical mechanics to derive universal scaling laws.
result: They identify distinct depth-dependent regimes and show that the anticoncentration behavior is universal across different circuit architectures, depending only on the noise rate and depth.
conclusion: The findings provide a unified framework for predicting when noisy quantum circuits exhibit anticoncentration, which is essential for validating quantum supremacy experiments and understanding the transition to classical simulability.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments relevant to NV centers.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum sensing and quantum information processing, but existing methods are often slow or limited to low dimensions.
method: The authors develop a scalable variational Bayesian inference approach that performs joint model selection and parameter estimation, and integrate it with real-time adaptive measurement strategies.
result: The framework accurately identifies unknown spin environments and supports adaptive measurements, demonstrating fast and scalable performance in high-dimensional quantum systems.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides a powerful tool for quantum system characterization, with potential applications in quantum sensing and quantum network nodes.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but loading and imaging them typically causes atom loss and heating. The authors aim to improve the fidelity and efficiency of these processes.
method: They employ electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) to achieve nondestructive imaging and loading of atoms in a continuously operated array, working in finite magnetic fields.
result: The technique enables high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays, as demonstrated in the paper.
conclusion: This work advances the practical capabilities of neutral-atom quantum computing platforms by improving the loading and imaging processes.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions for enhanced parameter estimation, bridging quantum sensing and critical phenomena.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a route to surpass classical limits in parameter estimation, which is of fundamental interest in quantum metrology and thermodynamics.
method: The paper provides a pedagogical review of parameter estimation theory (Fisher information, Cramér-Rao bound) and its application to systems near quantum phase transitions, discussing various models and techniques.
result: It consolidates known results and provides a framework for understanding how criticality enhances sensing, highlighting trade-offs and practical considerations.
conclusion: Quantum critical systems are promising for high-precision sensing, but practical challenges remain; the tutorial serves as a guide for future research.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an open-source pulse-optimization framework for high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates in neutral-atom platforms, targeting quantum error correction applications.
motivation: Multiqubit gates are essential for efficient quantum error correction, but achieving high fidelity in neutral-atom platforms is challenging. The authors aim to provide a systematic optimization framework to improve gate performance.
method: They develop an open-source pulse-optimization framework that optimizes control pulses for multiqubit Rydberg gates, likely using numerical optimization techniques to maximize gate fidelity while considering experimental constraints.
result: The framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates, as demonstrated through simulations or experiments, showing improved performance for quantum error correction applications.
conclusion: The proposed framework offers a practical tool for designing high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom quantum computing, advancing the feasibility of quantum error correction on these platforms.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies a deep spin defect in ZnO with long coherence and high spin selectivity, enabling high-fidelity single-shot readout for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: To find new solid-state platforms for quantum information processing, particularly defects with long coherence and efficient readout, as alternatives to NV centers in diamond.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations to identify a deep-level defect in ZnO with small electron-phonon coupling, and characterize its spin properties and readout fidelity.
result: The defect exhibits a 4-ms spin coherence time and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishing ZnO as a viable platform for quantum technologies.
conclusion: ZnO defects are promising for scalable quantum information processing, offering long coherence and high-fidelity readout.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a new variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra to improve quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving is a technique for fast quantum control, but variational approaches often suffer from low fidelity. The authors aim to enhance fidelity by designing a better variational ansatz.
method: They propose a new variational counterdiabatic driving scheme that incorporates weighted actions and uses computer algebra to optimize the control parameters, likely by constructing a more flexible ansatz for the counterdiabatic Hamiltonian.
result: The method achieves higher fidelity compared to existing variational counterdiabatic driving approaches, as demonstrated in numerical examples.
conclusion: The proposed technique offers a readily available upgrade to current variational counterdiabatic driving methods, improving the performance of quantum control protocols.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: To overcome performance limits of traditional Josephson mixers, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale quantum processors.
method: The authors design and fabricate impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers, optimizing their bandwidth and saturation power through engineering of the Josephson junction array and circuit parameters.
result: The mixers demonstrate significantly improved bandwidth and saturation power, allowing for efficient quantum signal amplification and transduction.
conclusion: These enhanced mixers are promising components for scalable quantum information processing, particularly in hybrid quantum systems where microwave-to-optical transduction is needed.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: This review classifies universal behaviors in driven open quantum systems using nonequilibrium quantum field theory, focusing on symmetry, topology, and state purity.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, and understanding their universal nonequilibrium stationary states is crucial for advancing quantum thermodynamics and information processing.
method: The paper provides a theoretical review, synthesizing concepts from nonequilibrium quantum field theory, symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity to categorize universal behaviors.
result: It identifies distinct types of universality in driven open quantum matter, linking them to symmetry and topology, and discusses their implications for quantum state purity.
conclusion: The review establishes a framework for understanding universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, which is relevant for quantum thermodynamics and potentially quantum information applications.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods, particularly cluster expansion, for predicting decoherence times of solid-state spin qubits, highlighting their growing predictive power and remaining challenges.
motivation: Long coherence times are crucial for quantum technologies, and accurate prediction of decoherence is essential for designing spin qubits. The paper aims to assess the current state and future directions of computational approaches.
method: The authors review ab initio and cluster expansion techniques for calculating spin-spin relaxation times, discussing their applicability and limitations for various spin qubit systems.
result: Cluster expansion methods now provide reliable predictions for many spin qubit types, but challenges remain for cases involving higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational prediction of decoherence is becoming a reliable tool, but further development is needed to handle complex environments and improve accuracy.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review analyzes information-theoretic approaches and proposed tabletop experiments for testing whether gravity induces entanglement, potentially revealing non-classical features of gravity.
motivation: To address the fundamental question of whether gravity is classical or quantum by using information-theoretic methods, specifically gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) experiments.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks and analyzes various proposed tabletop-scale GIE experiments, focusing on how quantum information concepts can constrain possible theories of gravity.
result: It provides a status update on theoretical approaches and concrete experimental proposals for detecting GIE, highlighting their feasibility and potential to test quantum aspects of gravity.
conclusion: Information-theoretic methods offer a promising path to experimentally probe the quantum nature of gravity, with GIE experiments being a key candidate.

title: Collapse And Revival Of Exciton-Polaritons In A Single Nanocavity Revealed By Ultrafast Nonlinear Microscopy
authors: Liyu Zhang, Zhongao Huang, Kai Wang, Chao Guan, Zijian He, Jiaxing Yang, Shuzheng Chen, Xiaobo Han, And Peixiang Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Liyu Zhang, Zhongao Huang, Kai Wang, Chao Guan, Zijian He, Jiaxing Yang, Shuzheng Chen, Xiaobo Han, and Peixiang Lu

The ultrafast dynamics of exciton-polaritons (EPs) in single plasmonic nanocavities are of fundamental interest due to extreme mode confinement ([MATH]), which enables few-exciton strong coupling and strong nonlinearity of EPs. However, directly probing transient evolutions of EPs in a…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 056906] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ultrafast dynamics of exciton-polaritons in single plasmonic nanocavities, revealing collapse and revival phenomena via nonlinear microscopy.
motivation: Understanding the ultrafast dynamics of exciton-polaritons in strongly confined nanocavities is crucial for exploiting few-exciton strong coupling and nonlinearities for quantum technologies.
method: The authors employ ultrafast nonlinear microscopy to directly probe the transient evolution of exciton-polaritons in single plasmonic nanocavities.
result: They observe collapse and revival of exciton-polaritons, providing insights into the coherent dynamics and nonlinear interactions in these hybrid systems.
conclusion: The findings advance the understanding of exciton-polariton dynamics in nanocavities, which is relevant for developing hybrid quantum devices.

title: Nonreciprocal And Long-Range Three-Body Interactions In Bose-Einstein Condensates Induced By Optical Feedback
authors: Yi-Qing Zhang, Liang-Jun He, Han Pu, Zheng-Wei Zhou, And Yong-Chang Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yi-Qing Zhang, Liang-Jun He, Han Pu, Zheng-Wei Zhou, and Yong-Chang Zhang

We propose generating atom-atom three-body interactions in quantum gases by placing a quasi-two-dimensional Bose-Einstein condensate in front of two reflecting mirrors and illuminating it with dichromatic laser beams. These pumping fields traverse the condensate twice, thereby inducing a feedback ef…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 053201] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes generating long-range three-body interactions in a Bose-Einstein condensate using optical feedback from two mirrors, which could enable novel quantum simulation and information processing.
motivation: The authors aim to engineer strong, long-range three-body interactions in quantum gases, which are typically weak and short-range, to explore new quantum phases and applications.
method: They place a quasi-2D BEC in an optical cavity formed by two mirrors and illuminate it with dichromatic laser beams, causing feedback that induces effective three-body interactions between atoms.
result: The proposed scheme yields nonreciprocal and long-range three-body interactions, with tunable strength and range, as demonstrated through theoretical analysis.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method to realize exotic many-body interactions in ultracold atoms, opening avenues for quantum simulation and quantum information tasks.

title: Levitated Nano-accelerometer Sensitized By Quantum Quench
authors: M. Kamba, S. Otabe, K. Funo, T. Sagawa, And K. Aikawa
abstract:
Author(s): M. Kamba, S. Otabe, K. Funo, T. Sagawa, and K. Aikawa

We realize a nanoscale accelerometer with a levitated nanoparticle near the ground state, exploiting its dynamical behavior triggered by the abrupt quench of its trapping potential. We find that rapid quenching provides a readout time at which the sensitivity is enhanced by 2 orders of magnitude wit…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050801] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: A levitated nanoparticle near its ground state is used as a nanoscale accelerometer, with sensitivity enhanced by two orders of magnitude via a rapid quench of the trapping potential.
motivation: To improve the sensitivity of nanoscale accelerometers, which are important for force sensing and tests of quantum mechanics at macroscopic scales.
method: The authors experimentally realize a levitated nanoparticle in an optical trap, cool it near the ground state, and then abruptly quench the trapping potential to trigger dynamical behavior that enhances the readout sensitivity.
result: They demonstrate a sensitivity enhancement of two orders of magnitude at a specific readout time after the quench, achieving a nanoscale accelerometer with improved performance.
conclusion: The quantum quench technique provides a new way to enhance the sensitivity of levitated nanoparticle sensors, with potential applications in precision measurement and quantum technology.

title: Renormalization Of The Quantum Stress Tensor Fluctuations And The Limits Of Semiclassical Gravity
authors: Alejandro Perez And Daniel Sudarsky
abstract:
Author(s): Alejandro Perez and Daniel Sudarsky

We analyze the expectation value of the energy-momentum tensor and its fluctuations in quantum field theory on curved spacetimes. A generally accepeted condition for the conceptual consistency of semiclassical gravity is that the fluctuations of the energy momentum tensor remain small compared to it…
